mike (runtime): FYI ran a focused perf pass on kernel-path / KV-eviction interactions after the regression from yesterday, attaching quick numbers below.
anya (sre): saw the alert, thanks. what looks like the root cause?
mike (runtime): short: when KV eviction happens under microburst patterns the kernel selector sometimes picks the 'fast-single' path which has worse cold-KV latency. evictions + microbatch=tail spikes.
liam (perf): put the short table in the thread, added 99/95 percentiles from the profile run.
liam (perf): ```
config           | qps | microbatch | p95(ms) | p99(ms) | tp(tps)
fast-single + LRU | 100 | 8          | 180     | 520     | 900
vector-kernel + LRU|100 | 4          | 220     | 320     | 760
vector-kernel + warm|100| 4          | 200     | 280     | 745
quant-path + LRU   |100 | 8          | 195     | 400     | 920
```
priya (sales): customer asks for p95 <= 250ms and p99 <= 350ms at 100 qps. they said 'no carveouts' in the first pass. urgent meeting tomorrow.
jordan (product): that customer number (p99 350) is tough with current default microbatch=8 and our eviction settings. options: 1) lower microbatch to 4 for them (throughput hit), 2) dedicated pool with pinned warm KV, 3) prefer vector-kernel + proactive warmup, 4) SLA carveout for tail.
anya (sre): operationally, lowering microbatch from 8->4 drops throughput ~15-20% but stabilizes p99 in our tests. we can also tune KV TTL to avoid evictions during bursts.
mike (runtime): mechanics: the kernel selector uses a score = latency_est + cost_penalty; eviction increases latency_est intermittently and the selector oscillates. quick patch: add a transient-penalty when KV-miss rate > X to prefer vector-path for next N requests. prototype: `if kv_miss_rate > 0.03: prefer_kernel('vector', duration=3s)`
liam (perf): ran a canary with that transient-penalty and microbatch=6: p95=190ms p99=340ms at 100qps, tp -8%. stable across 30m.
priya (sales): that's promising. customer will accept a 10% throughput variance if p99 is met. they also asked how long it takes to roll.
mike (runtime): rollout: feature flag, canary 5% > 25% > 100% over 3 hours with automated rollback on p99 violation. code-side ~2 days to clean up, ops-runbook ~1 day.
jordan (product): can we offer them: vector-kernel + transient-penalty + microbatch=6 in a dedicated routing policy? then advertise p95/p99 guarantees.
anya (sre): yes but we should offer monitoring hooks: per-route kv-miss, kernel-switch-rate, and a baseline trace for tail traces. buildbot: deploy scheduled.
buildbot: deploy:trial/kv-penalty-canary -> SUCCESS (5% traffic) :thumbsup:
priya (sales): I'll tell customer we can try that as a targeted config with SLA terms to be discussed. will ask if they want dedicated or shared with config locks.
mike (runtime): followups: 1) add metric for kernel-selection-oscillation, 2) add automated warmup for vector-path on detected bursts, 3) adjust microbatch default heuristics to prefer smaller batches for short-seq workloads.
liam (perf): next profiling run scheduled in 2h, will post updated p95/p99 matrix including steady-state and burst scenarios.
jordan (product): thanks all — let's prep a short doc for Sales with the tradeoffs (p95 vs p99 vs throughput) and a suggested canary plan. Priya can you confirm customer timezone for tomorrow?
priya (sales): i have the meeting at 09:00 PDT, will push the canary notes and ask about appetite for dedicated pool.
mike (runtime): one caution: if customer refuses config changes, we should be prepared to propose reserved capacity commit. that's a quantifiable ask.
anya (sre): agreed. also adding an alert: if p99 > 360ms for 10m during canary -> auto rollback.
liam (perf): pasted the extended perf logs to the gcs link: https://gcs.redwood-internal/profiles/2149998888/run1.log
priya (sales): sharing w customer after the 09:00 call. thanks team. :pray:
mike (runtime): OK, will open a PR for the transient-penalty and microbatch knob. tagging @liam for benchmark review.
liam (perf): will review. thanks.
